quick_facts.label: What the job is
quick_facts.value: Purchasing managers plan, direct or coordinate the work of buyers, purchasing officers and related workers; the occupation includes procurement managers.

quick_facts.label: Other names for it
quick_facts.value: Job titles O*NET reports for this occupation (Purchasing Managers) include Procurement Manager, Purchasing Manager, Commodity Manager and Materials Manager.

quick_facts.label: Typical preparation
quick_facts.value: O*NET places this occupation in Job Zone Four (considerable preparation needed): most of these occupations require a four-year bachelor's degree, but some do not.

sections.heading: What a procurement manager does
paragraphs: Purchasing managers plan, direct or coordinate the work of buyers, purchasing officers and related workers; the occupation includes procurement managers.

The tasks below are taken from the O*NET profile for Purchasing Managers. O*NET is the US Department of Labor's occupation database, so this describes the job as it is profiled in the United States; titles and duties in Indian companies can differ.
bullets: Develop and apply purchasing and contract-management policies and procedures.
Find vendors and interview them about product availability and terms of sale.
Review, evaluate and approve specifications for issuing and awarding bids.
Check purchase-order claims and contracts against company policy.
